## The basics

[PubPeer](https://pubpeer.com/) is a website where researchers can leave public comments on published papers, usually to raise questions or concerns about the work. `ref_pubpeer` checks whether any of the papers a manuscript cites have comments on PubPeer, so you know a discussion exists before you rely on that citation.

Here is the module running on a demo paper, which cites a reference with PubPeer comments:


```{.r .cell-code}
paper <- demopaper()
module_run(paper, "ref_pubpeer")
```

PubPeer Comments: You cited 1 reference with comments in PubPeer.

Running a module always works the same way: `module_run(paper, "module_name")`. The printed result above is a short report: a coloured light and a one-line summary.

If you want to work with the result instead of just reading it, save it to a variable and look inside it:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mo <- module_run(paper, "ref_pubpeer")
mo$table[, c("doi", "total_comments", "url")] |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|doi                      | total_comments|url                                                             |
|:------------------------|--------------:|:---------------------------------------------------------------|
|10.1177/0956797614520714 |              3|https://pubpeer.com/publications/3FA648ECECB88454C91804F09E2E56 |


:::
:::


`mo$table` lists each cited reference that has PubPeer comments, how many, and a `url` to the discussion. A flagged result does not mean the citation is bad — it only means there is a discussion worth reading. Follow the `url`, read the comments yourself, and decide whether they matter for how the citation is used.

## What it checks

The `ref_pubpeer` module cross-references the paper's **cited references** against [PubPeer](https://pubpeer.com/), a platform for post-publication peer review. If a paper you cite has comments on PubPeer, that may be worth knowing — comments can range from minor clarifications to serious concerns about the work.

The module reports which cited references have PubPeer comments, how many, and a link, so you can read the discussion and judge its relevance yourself.

Statcheck comments on PubPeer are ignored. Statcheck automatically posted comments on [tens of thousands of psychology articles](https://retractionwatch.com/2016/09/02/heres-why-more-than-50000-psychology-studies-are-about-to-have-pubpeer-entries/), so including them would flag almost every cited paper and drown out substantive human comments.

::: callout-note
This module makes **live network calls** to PubPeer (matching references by DOI). You need an internet connection to run the code below.
:::

## Running the module

`demopaper()` cites a reference that has PubPeer comments.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
paper <- demopaper()
mo <- module_run(paper, "ref_pubpeer")
mo$traffic_light
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
#> [1] "info"
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
mo$summary_text
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
#> [1] "You cited 1 reference with comments in PubPeer."
```


:::
:::


The `table` lists each matched reference, the number of comments, and a link:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mo$table[, c("doi", "total_comments", "url")] |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|doi                      | total_comments|url                                                             |
|:------------------------|--------------:|:---------------------------------------------------------------|
|10.1177/0956797614520714 |              3|https://pubpeer.com/publications/3FA648ECECB88454C91804F09E2E56 |


:::
:::


## Running on many papers


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mo <- module_run(psychsci[1:10], "ref_pubpeer")
mo$summary_table
```
:::


## Interpreting the result

A `green`/empty result means none of the cited references had PubPeer comments. A flagged result does **not** mean a citation is bad — it means there is a discussion you may want to read. Follow the `url` to the PubPeer thread and judge the comments in context.

## Options

`ref_pubpeer` takes only the `paper` argument.

## Notes

In the Shiny app, querying PubPeer is an opt-in checkbox, because it sends the cited DOIs to an external service.
